title: Rule decision (schemaVersion 1.0.0)
description: Deterministic output of one evaluation. Every list has a pinned order so Python and TypeScript produce byte-identical results for the same request: acceptedObservationIds, unknownObservationKeys, and conflictingObservationKeys are sorted lexicographically by Unicode code point; rejectedObservations is sorted by observationId; actions, suppressedActions, notices, and timerOps follow rule-package declaration order. A decision proposes; adapters perform external effects only after their own authorization and revision checks.

reviewStatus.description: Review state of the package that produced this decision. Consumers must not present unreviewed_demo content as clinically validated.

guidanceActive.description: False when the mode policy suspends clinical progression, for example during handover.

nextStateRevision.description: stateRevision + 1 when stateChanged is true, otherwise unchanged.

code.description: unknown_observation_key: key outside the package catalog. invalid_value: value not valid for the declared type. source_cannot_confirm: a proposal source claimed a stronger confirmation than it can carry. insufficient_confirmation: confirmation below the key minimum, so the value cannot establish the fact.

resolvedObservations.description: Value actually used per catalog key. Every catalog key appears. A key with no usable observation, or with an unresolvable conflict, carries the literal string unknown; it never becomes false.

unknownObservationKeys.description: Catalog keys that resolved to unknown.

conflictingObservationKeys.description: Keys where equally ranked observations disagreed. Such keys resolve to unknown rather than to an arbitrary winner.

instruction.description: Rendered approved wording for the current step, or null when the mode suspends guidance.

actions.description: Action intents permitted under the current mode policy.

suppressedActions.description: Action intents withheld by the mode policy, reported rather than dropped silently.

op.description: start, stop, reset, pause, and resume come from the rule package. set_audible is emitted by the interpreter when an interaction-mode change must silence or unsilence a timer that keeps running, so elapsed treatment time is preserved.

audible.description: False means the timer still runs but produces no sound, for example during dispatcher guidance.

outputChannels.description: Channels the caller may use for this decision. Contains screen always, and audio only when the mode policy allows it.

text.description: Approved wording with declared placeholders substituted. Never generated prose.
